newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia peacekeepers deploy in southeast port.
newsitem.headline: Liberia peacekeepers deploy in southeast port.

text.p: West African peacekeepers left for Liberia's southeastern port of Greenville on Tuesday on their first major deployment outside the capital since civil war flared there in April and May, witnesses and officials said.
Earlier, reconciled faction leaders Alhaji Kromah and Roosevelt Johnson ordered a halt to all fighting between their supporters in the troubled southwestern Cape Mount County.

Four military helicopters carrying troops from the Nigerian-led ECOMOG force left Monrovia to launch the deployment in and around Greenville, an area where supporters of faction leader Charles Taylor have been fighting ethnic Krahn rivals.
Force officials said the helicopters would make two trips on Tuesday with a sea deployment later in the week. An advance unit went to Greenville last week.
Force commander Victor Malu warned faction fighters and their leaders against impeding the force's operations.
"ECOMOG is determined to succeed and will not allow any faction to sabotage its efforts but will take appropriate measures," he said in a statement on Monday.

General John Tarnue of Taylor's National Patriotic Front of Liberia was travelling to the port with the peacekeepers. "We believe this is the time to disarm and we are ready to do all we can to do just that. It's now time for the ballots and the time for hostilities is over," he said before leaving.

West African leaders rallied the faction leaders around yet another peace plan in Nigeria in August. It envisaged disarmament by January and elections by May, with the threat of individual sanctions against anyone derailing the deal.
A battalion of over 1,000 men is expected to deploy in and around the port, where militia groups are suspected of exporting gold and timber illegally.
But ECOMOG Chief of Staff General Abdou Mohammed said their duties would extend to opening up highways to the ports of Harper near the border with Ivory Coast and Buchanan.
"They will carry out daily patrols in those areas," said Greenville battalion commander Lieutenant-Colonel Luka Yusuf.

Malu, promised reinforcements to double ECOMOG's strength to 18,000, had previously said he would not deploy further outside Monrovia until extra men arrived. The force patrols main roads to hot spots in the west and is in Kakata north of Monrovia, Buchanan port and Harbel in the east.
Freed American slaves set up Liberia in 1847. The war, launched by Taylor in late 1989, is rooted in rivalry between descendents of the slaves and the original inhabitants.
It has killed well over 150,000 people, hundreds of them in fighting and looting in Monrovia in April and May.

Kromah and Johnson, who lead the rival Mandingo and Krahn wings of the ULIMO movement that was originally set up to fight Taylor, agreed at the weekend to create a buffer zone between their forces in Cape Mount to be patrolled by ECOMOG.
